trust_decision.summary: Decided in the serializer when an IRI is resolved: the object returned for an IRI must be an instance of the resource class declared for the slot - is_a($item, $resourceClass) on the whole-document IRI branch and is_a($item, $className) in the relation branch. The IRI converter's own is_a guard only fires when the caller passes an Operation, which neither caller does.

landing_point.why: The summary says relation IRIs are not type-checked, so the first place an engineer looks is denormalizeRelation(), the method that turns a relation's IRI string into an object with no comparison against the declared $className.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP item write whose request body is itself an IRI (any denormalizing format: json, jsonld, jsonapi, graphql), or the public SerializerInterface::deserialize()/denormalize() call with an IRI string
HTTP item write carrying a relation IRI (single relation and, via denormalizeCollection at :587/:598, each element of a relation collection), including GraphQL mutation input

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The IRI converter already carries the is_a guard (:86) so the converter is left alone and the flaw reads as callers forgetting to pass an Operation, while JSON:API linkage already demands a type member (:213) so that transport looks type-checked too.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A relation declared as an abstract resource class or interface must still accept an IRI resolving to a concrete subclass (discriminator fixtures AbstractDummy/ConcreteDummy); a fix that compares the effective class for equality, instead of the is_a() idiom the project itself uses, rejects legitimate polymorphic relations.

O6_input_shapes: bare IRI string as the whole denormalized document (\is_string($data) branch)
IRI string as the value of a single relation property
IRI string as an element of a to-many relation collection (denormalizeCollection -> denormalizeRelation)

O7_producer.where: src/Serializer/AbstractItemNormalizer.php:955 (relation class taken from property builtin types, resolved by ResourceClassResolver::getResourceClass)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: JSON:API relationship linkage ({type,id} or a list of them) is resolved by the JsonApi ItemNormalizer's own denormalizeRelation override, which calls getResourceFromIri and returns the object with no is_a check against $className
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: JSON:API linkage always carries a type member and the override only adapts the document shape, so the transport looks type-checked and is read as a separate concern the JSON-LD advisory never covered

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The id member of a JSON request body is resolved to the object to populate without passing the operation, so the IRI's resource class is never compared with the class being denormalized
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: it is the update/object-to-populate path, not a relation, so it is argued to be outside a relation-IRI advisory

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The data.id member of a JSON:API document is resolved to the object to populate without passing the operation or comparing its class with the operation's class
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: same as above - it is the update path, and JSON:API's declared type member is assumed to settle the type

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an override that checks the class of the object resolved from the body's id before it becomes OBJECT_TO_POPULATE
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same getResourceFromIri primitive is already called there twice, and harden-the-callers is exactly the strategy the published fix chose

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the operation/class guard that the Symfony converter has at :86, added to the Laravel converter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the Laravel converter is a hand-copied second implementation of the same interface that never got the is_a guard, so a maintainer closing this advisory would plausibly mirror it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a class check on IRI parameter values (single and array) before setValue()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: same IRI-to-object primitive used by parameter providers; a maintainer hardening 'an IRI must reference the declared class' could apply it here

O10_build.toolchain: PHP >=8.2, Composer monorepo (root plus per-package composer.json), PHPUnit via phpunit.xml.dist, Symfony 6.4/7.x, Doctrine ORM for the functional app
O10_build.project_tests: src/Serializer/Tests/AbstractItemNormalizerTest.php (relation denormalization tests around :893 and :1032-1100) and src/JsonApi/Tests/Serializer/ItemNormalizerTest.php:280-360 (linkage denormalization); the functional ApiTestCase suite for this fix is new - tests/Functional/Security does not exist at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Pass the root operation into IriConverter::getResourceFromIri so the existing is_a guard fires - which compares the root operation's class, not the relation's declared class - and guard only denormalizeRelation, the method the report names.

out_of_scope_notes: GraphQl ReadProvider:76 compares the operation class to the item class only for Subscription/Mutation, never for Query - a read-side class mismatch outside this write-side advisory; not pursued.
Doctrine search filters resolve filter values as IRIs with no class check (src/Doctrine/Common/Filter/SearchFilterTrait.php:125); read-side, outside this advisory's protection; not pursued.
